chunks: 2742 - And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man performs tamattuʿ, then forgets to trim until he enters into iḥrām for hajj. So he said: “He must offer a sacrifice.”
And in the narration of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام:
“He should seek forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted.”

key_terms.دَمٌ: a sacrificial offering due as expiation
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: to trim the hair as part of release from iḥrām
key_terms.يُهِلَّ بِالْحَجِّ: to begin the iḥrām and rite of hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone performing tamattuʿ hajj who forgets to trim before entering iḥrām for hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the mutamattiʿ who forgets to trim the hair before beginning the iḥrām of hajj. One report states that a sacrificial offering is due, while another report instructs him to seek forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2742 - Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Abu Ibrahim (as):

I asked him about a man performing tamattu‘ (Hajj) who forgets to trim his hair until he has already entered the state of ihram for Hajj.
Imam (as) said: "He must offer a sacrifice."
In another narration, Abdullah ibn Sinan reported from Abu Abdullah (as):
"He should seek forgiveness from Allah (swt), the Exalted."
